1	# Task 10: Click-to-plant garden that grows over time
2	
3	Build a single-page browser app with the provided framework, served by vite, rendering to the canvas with id #app. The app is an interactive 3D garden. A flat ground plane (soil or grass) fills the lower part of the view, with a soft sky or background behind it and a camera looking down at it from an angle so the whole plot is visible.
4	
5	When the user clicks on the ground, a new plant must be planted at the exact spot that was clicked (the click must be mapped to the ground, not just to the screen centre). Each plant starts as a tiny sprout and grows smoothly over about 8 seconds into a mature plant (for example a stem with leaves and a flower or a small bush) that is visibly larger, with a different shape or colour from the sprout. Plants must keep growing independently, so a plant planted later is smaller than one planted earlier. Vary the flower colour or size between plants so a full garden does not look uniform. Support at least 40 plants at once without dropping below a smooth frame rate, and ignore clicks that do not hit the ground.
6	
7	Add a small on-screen DOM overlay in a corner showing the text 'Plants: N' where N is the current plant count, and a 'Clear' button that removes all plants. The scene should have lighting and soft shadows so plants look grounded, and it should render correctly on first load with no console errors and with zero plants planted.
8

I'm working out the camera placement and ground plane sizing so clicks outside the plot bounds get ignored while anything landing within the visible ground area triggers planting.

For rendering, I'm considering a fixed-capacity instance pool approach—allocating enough stem, leaf, petal, and center instances to cover a few hundred plants, scaling unused ones to zero rather than dynamically resizing arrays each frame, since I'm unsure if the instancing API tolerates variable counts cleanly.

I'm now sketching the plant growth stages: sprouts start as tiny stems with cotyledon leaves, maturing into taller stems with more leaves and a flower head whose petals fade in once growth passes the halfway point, all driven by an eased time-based progress value.

Working out petal placement...

For leaves, I'll use ellipsoid scaling with yaw-only rotation, skipping tilt to avoid euler order ambiguity, and rely on directional shadows with default casting enabled. Now I'm figuring out per-plant state tracking like position and planted timestamp.

Growth will be computed as age/8 clamped to 1, exposed linearly for tests but visually eased with smoothstep, using accumulated frame delta time as the clock. I'm making __TASK_STATE__ read-only by defining it with a getter via Object.defineProperty.

Working out the click-to-world mapping now: converting canvas coordinates to NDC, building camera basis vectors from forward/right/up, constructing the ray direction using FOV and aspect ratio, then intersecting with the ground plane at y=0 and checking it falls within bounds.

Checking whether the camera setup (position at height 15, distance 17, 45° fov) actually keeps the full 24x24 ground plane visible within the viewport, accounting for the tilt angle and foreshortening near the far edge.

Finding that at the original distances the near edge falls outside the view frustum, so I'm adjusting the camera to [0,20,24] and rechecking the pitch angle and corner visibility for both near and far edges, then working out the horizontal field of view at those depths.

Settling on a ground plane sized around 22x22 (half-extent 11), rechecked against the frustum angles so it stays visible with sky above the horizon, and I'll treat anything within that half-extent as plantable while ignoring clicks beyond it.

For the background I'll just use a flat sky-blue scene color rather than a gradient helper, paired with soft default shadows, mutable instance nodes I can update via setInstances with initial hidden transforms and white colors, and a simple DOM overlay with text and a clear button.

I'll cap plants around 150 with proportional stem/leaf/petal/center instance counts, rebuilding transform arrays only when something's actively growing or dirty to avoid unnecessary per-frame allocation, with hidden instances tucked below the scene at near-zero scale.

For the plant geometry itself, I'm working out stem height and radius as functions of growth progress and overall size, using smoothstep easing so stems thicken and extend naturally; leaves are modeled as four units where the first two appear early as small cotyledons and the remaining two scale in later during growth.

Still writing geometry logic...

I'm figuring out how petal colors and counts vary per plant, and planning how leaf/stem color arrays get stored and updated per instance when plants are planted or cleared.

For randomness I'll use a seeded generator for deterministic flower colors picked from a fixed palette, plus figuring out readiness signaling and wiring up a click listener on the canvas for planting via an orbit camera.

I need to confirm the canvas CSS size for proper click-to-world mapping, and I'm placing the overlay UI with pointer-events so button clicks don't bubble into the canvas's plant-on-click handler since the button sits outside the canvas element.

input.summary:
I wrote src/main.ts for the garden app, but I couldn't check it against the engine. The typecheck tool reports one error: `@aura3d/engine` is missing from the sandbox's node_modules (the folder doesn't exist). I never saw the package's types, so the engine calls come from the docs. The build and the browser behaviour are untested.

- **Scene:** a 22×22 grass plane under a fixed perspective camera at [0, 20, 24] looking at the origin, with a pale sky background, a hemisphere light, a shadow-casting directional light and light fog.
- **Plants:** four instanced meshes (stems, leaves, petals, flower centres) are rebuilt only while a plant is still growing or after a change. Each plant has its own start time and grows over 8 seconds with smoothstep easing. It starts as a short stem with two small seed leaves and ends as a taller stem with four leaves and a flower. Flower colour, centre colour, leaf green, size and rotation vary per plant.
- **Clicking:** a click on the canvas is turned into a ray from the camera and intersected with the plane y=0. Clicks that miss the ground or fall outside the plane are ignored.
- **Overlay and globals:** a top-left box shows "Plants: N" and a Clear button. `window.__TASK_STATE__` is a read-only getter returning `{plantCount, plants[{x, z, growth}], ready}`, and `window.__plantAt(x, z)` plants at a ground position. `window.__EVAL_READY__` is set after `app.ready()`.

Things that may not work as written:
- The click-to-ground maths assumes `fov` is the vertical field of view in degrees. If the engine defines it differently, plants will land off the click.
- I call `setInstances` with `?.`, so if the engine doesn't provide it on runtime nodes, no plants will appear.
- The garden holds at most 150 plants. Further plants are ignored.
